audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says Irelia's W "blocks" your big Q autos and tells you not to throw a fat Q she can block, but never says what W is, what it actually does, or how long it is unavailable afterwards.
audit.why: Defiant Dance is a charged strike during which Irelia takes reduced PHYSICAL damage. Siphoning Strike is physical, so a stacked Q dumped into the charge is the single most expensive mistake available in this lane — it is not a block or a dodge, it is damage reduction that scales with how long she holds it. It is 20/18/16/14/12s, the longest cooldown in her basic kit, so waiting the charge out and hitting her afterwards is a real, repeatable window.
audit.corrected: Named Defiant Dance, gave the physical-damage-reduction reason and the 20s/12s cooldown, and turned it into a wait-then-Q sequencing cue in early, mid, breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json (W Defiant Dance: "She takes reduced physical damage during the charge", cd 20/18/16/14/12)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeats that she "resets through the minion wave" without ever stating the condition on the reset.
audit.why: Bladesurge refreshes its cooldown only if the target dies to it or is Marked, and Marks come from Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge. That makes the reset chain conditional and therefore deniable: a healthy wave and a dodged E leave Bladesurge on its full 10/9/8/7/6s.
audit.corrected: Stated the refresh condition in tldr and content mid so the player knows what to deny rather than just fearing the dash.
sources: champ-data/_kits/irelia.json (Q Bladesurge: "If the target is Marked or dies to Bladesurge, its cooldown refreshes", cd 10/9/8/7/6; E Flawless Duet Marks; R Vanguard's Edge Marks)

audit.whatIsWrong: full breakdown.cooldowns lists Flawless Duet twice — once as "Irelia Flawless Duet (Stun)" and again as "Irelia Flawless Duet" — and gives no number for either.
audit.why: One of the two lines is pure duplication, and the slot is better spent on the second cooldown that actually governs Nasus's damage, Defiant Dance. Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s.
audit.corrected: Replaced the duplicate with Defiant Dance and put real numbers on both.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere, though the entry's whole plan is to win extended fights.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals Irelia on every cast, and with resets that is a repeating heal through exactly the long grind this entry tells the player to aim for. _missing-interactions.json flags this rule for nasus vs irelia.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[4].why says level 6 is "the first real fight you're allowed to take" and that the stat-check runs your way, while its own side field says Irelia and content whys[4] says you survive but do not own it.
audit.why: Two layers of the same matchup give opposite advice about whether to fight at 6. The content layer is the conservative and correct one against a champion whose dash resets survive a Wither.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[4].why to match its side label and the content layer.

edits.before: - Irelia Flawless Duet (Stun): matchup-defining — Her engage CC. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Irelia Flawless Duet: Sends two blades that converge to stun — her engage CC. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Irelia Flawless Duet: matchup-defining — her engage stun, 16s at rank 1 and 10s maxed. Dodge it, then walk at her. - Irelia Defiant Dance: 20s at rank 1, the charge soaks physical damage — hold the stacked Q till it ends.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Flawless Duet (Stun): when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve her.
edits.after: Trade around Defiant Dance: the charge soaks physical damage, so hold the stacked Q until it ends, then hit her. If ahead, freeze and starve her.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands flips dives: pop R, Wither Irelia, and suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands buys survival, not a kill: R plus Wither answers one all-in, but her Bladesurge resets still edge the straight trade.

edits.before: Her resets + shred bully you — deny Q targets, Wither, out-scale. Nasus wins by trading around Irelia's Flawless Duet (Stun) and cashing the pattern: deny resets, Wither, out-scale.
edits.after: Her resets + shred bully you — deny Q targets, Wither, out-scale. Bladesurge refreshes only on a Marked or dying target, so a healthy wave and a dodged E strand her.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are genuinely even — neither of us wants to commit, so just last-hit with Q and chunk the wave with Spirit Fire for stacks and a little armor shred on her. The danger spikes the instant she hits 2: her Q resets through the minion line to gap-close, and with E stun plus passive shred she out-trades you hard. Do not throw a fat Q she can just block with W, and never sit in her Q-dash range without Wither — at this stage you have no kiting tool and your lifesteal alone won't out-heal her combo.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are genuinely even — neither of us wants to commit, so last-hit with Q and chunk the wave with Spirit Fire for stacks and a little armor shred on her. The danger spikes the instant she hits 2: Bladesurge (Q) resets through the minion line to gap-close, and with Flawless Duet (E) plus Ionian Fervor stacks she out-trades you hard. Never feed a fat Siphoning Strike into Defiant Dance (W) — the charge soaks physical damage and your Q is physical, so wait it out and hit her the moment it ends.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are the worst of it: she has Wither's answer (Q dashes) before you have Wither's payoff, and her armor shred makes your fat HP feel like paper. Play not to die — shove with Spirit Fire, soak Q stacks, and give up the plates if you must. Six is your lifeline: Fury of the Sands' bonus HP and AoE plus Wither lets you survive or even flip a committed all-in. Slow her with W the moment she dashes in so her Q-resets can't kite you, then R and grind. You still don't own the lane at 6, but you stop dying for free.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are the worst of it: Bladesurge refreshes whenever it kills its target or the target is Marked, so a low wave plus Flawless Duet gives her endless dashes while you have no kiting tool. Play not to die — shove with Spirit Fire, soak Q stacks, and give up the plates if you must. Six is your lifeline: Fury of the Sands' bonus HP and resistances plus Wither let you survive or even flip a committed all-in. Slow her the frame she dashes in, hold the stacked Q until Defiant Dance ends, then grind. You still don't own the lane at 6, but you stop dying for free.

edits.after: Survive to stack Q uncontested, and buy Grievous Wounds — Bladesurge heals her every reset

edits.after: Even with Fury of the Sands and Wither up, Bladesurge resets and a charged Defiant Dance let her edge the trade — you survive it.
